title: Add portable agent defaults and project overrides
description: Replace the bootstrap-only root configuration with a portable project configuration directory and a versioned built-in agent bundle. Yoyodyne must be usable from other project repositories without access to the Yoyodyne source checkout: the executable supplies complete default configurations and personas for product manager, architect, development manager, developer, and reviewer, while each project stores only its machine-independent settings and sparse agent overrides under .yoyodyne/. Add brief override instructions to README.md and a detailed configuration guide under docs/.
design: Embed a read-only builtin:v1 bundle in the executable, represented as declarative configuration and Markdown persona files rather than Go string constants. Keep non-bypassable authority, sandbox, review-verdict, integration, and cleanup rules enforced in Go; configured personas may specialize behavior but cannot remove those invariants. Discover the nearest .yoyodyne/config.yaml from the current directory upward, while continuing to accept an explicit --config path and the legacy .yoyodyne.yaml shape for compatibility. The project config declares extends: builtin:v1 and overlays the built-in bundle by stable agent name. Missing agent fields inherit; supplied scalar fields replace; persona overrides replace the complete inherited persona; instances remain validated; disabled: true explicitly removes an inherited agent; unknown fields, unknown built-in bundles, invalid role/backend combinations, absolute persona paths, traversal, and symlink escape fail closed. Resolve project persona paths within the project .yoyodyne directory, and record enough provenance in the effective config to explain whether a value came from the built-in bundle or project file. Wire effective developer and reviewer personas into their existing prompts without allowing project text into immutable harness policy. Migrate this repository to .yoyodyne/config.yaml and remove .yoyodyne.yaml. Provide config show --effective and --origins output suitable for diagnosing inheritance. Tracked README and docs files follow the repository-document Markdown rules: no ai-output front matter or tl-dr section.
acceptance_criteria: Yoyodyne runs from a repository containing only a minimal .yoyodyne/config.yaml that extends builtin:v1; all five default agent types have nonempty role, Claude Code backend, model selector, instance count, and versioned persona; a project can override one field or one persona without copying unrelated defaults; disabled: true removes an inherited optional agent but validation still requires the executable developer/reviewer roles needed by the invoked workflow; effective configuration and value origins are inspectable; prompt construction uses the effective persona while immutable developer/reviewer safety contracts remain enforced; configuration discovery works from the project root and a nested directory; explicit config and legacy complete-file compatibility are tested; invalid inheritance, unknown keys, unsafe persona paths, and invalid effective configs fail closed; README.md contains a short override example and links to a detailed docs/configuration.md guide covering layout, precedence, merge/removal semantics, persona rules, portability, migration, and inspection; this repository uses .yoyodyne/config.yaml; make check, make build, config validation, git diff --check, gofmt, and bd lint pass.
notes:
Sequencing directive (2026-08-16): implement this cross-cutting portable configuration foundation before the rest of Milestone 2/3 so subsequent Yoyodyne development can use shipped agent defaults and project overrides. It still directly supports the configurable management-role milestone.

title: Handle concurrent integration contention on a shared target branch
description: Adversarial review of PR #3 traced two runs racing to fast-forward the same target branch. Both promotion paths fail closed under contention -- the in-primary 'git merge --ff-only' hits index lock contention, and the non-checked-out path's 'update-ref' compare-and-swap loses the race on the old-value mismatch -- so no corruption or force-advance is possible. The gap is liveness, not safety: the losing run fails its whole pipeline rather than re-reading the moved target and retrying. Unreachable today because execution.max_concurrent_developers defaults to 1, but it becomes live as soon as this epic raises it.
design: Decide between serializing integration behind a harness-held lock and letting a losing run re-derive the target and retry a bounded number of times. Retry must re-run the ErrTargetDrift check against the newly observed target rather than reusing the recorded base commit, so a retry can never turn a drifted target into a silent overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: A run that loses an integration race retries or defers instead of failing outright; a test drives two concurrent Integrate calls against one target and asserts exactly one promotion, no lost commit, and no force-advance.

title: Let the product manager research and evaluate operator ideas
description: Give the product-manager role a governed workflow for considering ideas proposed by the operator. The product manager can clarify the idea, gather relevant evidence from configured capabilities such as web search, compare the evidence and proposal against the product brief, goals, directives, and known constraints, and recommend adoption, rejection, deferral, or an experiment. Research is advisory: it must not silently turn an idea into an approved goal, design, or implementation directive.
design: Keep research capabilities separate from product-manager authority. Evidence sources and tools are configurable and permissioned. Preserve source URLs or identifiers, retrieval time, material claims, uncertainty, counterevidence, and the reasoning behind the recommendation. Treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence rather than instructions. Store the evaluation durably and route any proposed brief, goal, or design change through the existing artifact-governance and approval workflow. Bound research by configurable privacy, cost, time, and source policies, and report when adequate evidence cannot be obtained.
acceptance_criteria: The operator can present an idea conversationally; the product manager asks necessary clarifying questions, uses configured research tools when evidence would help, cites discoverable sources, distinguishes facts from inference and uncertainty, evaluates alignment with the current brief and goals, and produces a durable recommendation. The evaluation can propose follow-up work or governed artifact changes, but no canonical brief, goal, design, directive, or implementation work is changed or created as approved work without the applicable policy and approval path.

title: Validate the built-in bundle's declared schema version
